_note: Curated, version-controlled subset for the CyberRisk demo. Titles follow the public framework names; descriptions are project-authored paraphrases. Not an official or certified assessment.

frameworks.name: NIST CSF
frameworks.description: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 (curated subset of subcategories).
controls: The organizational mission informs cybersecurity risk management priorities.
Risk management objectives are agreed by stakeholders and drive security decisions.
Cybersecurity roles and responsibilities are defined
Roles, responsibilities and authorities for cybersecurity are established and communicated.
Policy for managing cybersecurity risk is established, communicated and enforced.
Supply chain risk is integrated into risk management
Cybersecurity supply chain risk management is part of enterprise risk processes.
Inventories of hardware managed by the organization are maintained.
Inventories of software, services and systems are maintained.
Vulnerabilities in assets are identified and recorded
Vulnerabilities are identified, validated and recorded.
Threat intelligence is received from information sharing sources.
Risk is prioritized using threats, vulnerabilities and impact
Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods and impacts inform inherent risk and prioritization.
Improvements are identified from assessments and audits.
Identities and credentials for authorized users and services are managed.
Users, services and hardware are authenticated, with stronger methods for higher risk.
Access permissions and authorizations are managed with least privilege and separation of duties.
Personnel are provided awareness and training to perform cybersecurity tasks.
The confidentiality, integrity and availability of data at rest are protected.
The confidentiality, integrity and availability of data in transit are protected.
Software is maintained, replaced and removed commensurate with risk.
Log records are generated and made available for continuous monitoring.
Networks are protected from unauthorized access
Networks and environments are protected from unauthorized logical access and usage.
Networks and network services are monitored to find potentially adverse events.
Personnel activity and technology usage are monitored to find potentially adverse events.
Computing hardware and software are monitored
Computing hardware, software and their data are monitored for adverse events.
Potentially adverse events are analyzed to better understand associated activities.
The incident response plan is executed
The incident response plan is executed in coordination with relevant parties.
Analysis is performed to establish what has taken place and the root cause.
Internal and external stakeholders are notified of incidents.
The recovery portion of the incident response plan is executed once initiated.
Recovery activities and progress are communicated to stakeholders.

frameworks.name: ISO/IEC 27001
frameworks.description: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A (control titles only; paraphrased summaries; no standard text reproduced).
controls: Information security policy and topic-specific policies are defined, approved and reviewed.
Inventory of information and other associated assets
An inventory of information and associated assets with owners is maintained.
Rules to control physical and logical access are established and implemented.
Security risks of supplier relationships are managed.
Incident management processes, roles and responsibilities are planned.
Incidents are responded to according to documented procedures.
ICT readiness is planned and tested against continuity objectives.
Information security awareness, education and training
Personnel receive appropriate security awareness and training.
Allocation and use of privileged access rights are restricted and managed.
Secure authentication technologies and procedures are implemented.
Protection against malware is implemented and supported by user awareness.
Information about technical vulnerabilities is obtained, evaluated and acted on.
Backup copies are maintained and regularly tested.
Logs recording activities and events are produced, stored and protected.
Networks, systems and applications are monitored for anomalous behaviour.
Networks and network devices are secured, managed and controlled.
Rules for effective use of cryptography are defined and implemented.
Changes to information processing facilities and systems follow change management.

frameworks.name: SOC 2
frameworks.description: AICPA SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria (curated subset of common criteria; paraphrased).
controls: Commitment to integrity and ethical values
The entity demonstrates a commitment to integrity and ethical values.
The entity obtains and uses relevant, quality information for internal control.
The entity identifies risks to its objectives and analyzes them as a basis for managing them.
The entity performs ongoing and/or separate evaluations of internal control.
The entity selects and develops general control activities over technology.
Logical access security software, infrastructure and architectures protect information assets.
New users are registered and authorized before credentials are issued.
Access is granted, modified and removed based on roles and least privilege.
Logical access security measures protect against threats from outside system boundaries.
Transmission and movement of information is restricted to authorized parties.
Controls prevent or detect unauthorized or malicious software.
Detection and monitoring procedures identify vulnerabilities and configuration changes.
Systems are monitored for anomalies indicative of malicious acts or errors.
Security events are evaluated to determine whether they are incidents.
Identified security incidents are responded to through a defined program.
Changes to infrastructure, data, software and procedures are authorized and tested.
Risks associated with vendors and business partners are assessed and managed.
Environmental protections, backup and recovery infrastructure are in place and tested.
